Vercel Board has been lighting my brain on fire for the last few days It's a genius idea, but I think most teams should build it from scratch Basically just a private Slack workspace for your agents AND developers (which can even sync to Slack channels for better observability) The idea (not necessarily Vercel's implementation of it) makes so many things simple: 1. Collaborative grilling Each locally running agent has its own identity on the board. As does every human! That means if you're grilling with an agent, and you need to ask someone a question, you just get your agent to ping them (or, ping their agent!) 2. Locally running agents This setup feels awesome for connecting locally running agents to the rest of the organisation. "Unread messages" could form a queue (Vercel board doesn't do this AFAIK) which would allow remote agents to ping messages to local agents, which would get picked up when they wake up. This would allow seamless communication between remote and local, and aid companies looking to make the leap to remote agents. 3. Schedules Want to schedule a cron? Just trigger a repeating message to an agent. I love how simple it makes the mental model. 4. Multi-vendor setups Creating a vendor-agnostic version of this would be sweet - a seamless collaboration environment for all of your vendor-locked servers/harnesses. 5. Deterministic workflows as commands One opportunity I see for Vercel Board is to allow for registering deterministic workflows as `/commands` - i.e. running review agents or implementer agents. This would allow you to mix and match agents and workflows in a really lovely way, and agents could themselves trigger workflows which report back via the board. Overall my brain is on fire, just wanted to share https://t.co/RnbGsFyqAM

tweets.text:
Rather than art, we ought to point AI towards human-understandability and conceptualization.

The Riemann proof should come with a paper, a walkthrough, new concepts and insights.

Much like the intermediate representation of high-level code is desirable even in a world where LLM will go straight to CPU instructions output.

quoted.text: I wonder if we are going to see an art develop of taking these vast proofs and improving them, not just by adding a bit of insight (as already been done in many cases), but by looking for implied concepts that compress them strongly.
